Pros: Very experienced in programming, vast knowledge in what he's doing and able to address any issue you bring to him with great expertise. Enthusiastic way of conducting class Interesting approach to helping students understand computing concepts Hilarious Records all of his lectures Gives you a reasonable amount of time for all projects Skateboards to class and plays guitar Cons: His lab programs are too hard to finish on time, but reform is in the works for this. Frequently goes off topic. His tangents are very entertaining, though! Reed is an excellent professor. Some people may say his approach to teaching is naive, but I think it is extremely insightful. He often compares programming methods to real life situations, which makes it much easier to understand. He will spend time with you out of class to help you with problems on your programs, and sincerely cares about his students -- enough to even pay for their Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) membership if special circumstances make it difficult to do so. He strongly believes in collaborative programming, and learning from discussing with others, rather than just listening to a lecture. I have not taken any of his tests yet, but so far the programs have taken me about 10 hours of total input to complete. Also for the people who are complaining about the TA's he is assigned, as of last year he was paired up with an excellent TA, Sean Deitz. He looks like he's straight out of Lord of the Rings but damn, he's helpful and brilliant. He is also extremely laid back and helps you through problems, rather than solves them for you. Note: This class is now taught in C/C++ with an emphasis on C (in order to teach you the underlying foundation of C++, and the power of C to create ultra-compact programs and directly manipulate memory addresses, etc.)
Pros:HUGE curve Cons:tests are hard Professor Reed is awesome, very charismatic

Pros:He looks nice for his age. Cons:He spends 30 minutes of the class talking about his life story, 15 minutes about random CS stuff and 5 minutes lecturing the material. His projects are awfully hard. I don't think the material given is for a beginner programmer because only the experienced ones were able to achieve an A. His TA's usually do not have English as their first language, so be prepared.

Great professor! By far the best teaching style I've seen for computer science. His explanations are superb and he encourages the class to ask questions if they don't understand something.
